html:
The Battle for Mexico City was a series of fights from 8 to 15 September 1847 in and around Mexico City. A United States army under General Winfield Scott took the capital from the Mexican forces of General Antonio López de Santa Anna. It was the last major battle of the Mexican-American War.

The war began in 1846 over Texas and the American wish for California. American victories in the north did not make Mexico give in, so Scott landed at Veracruz in March 1847 and marched inland. By September he stood outside the capital with about 7,000 men. On 13 September his troops stormed the hilltop castle of Chapultepec, home of the military academy, whose young cadets are remembered in Mexico as the Boy Heroes. The same day the Americans fought through two city gates. Santa Anna left in the night, and Scott entered on 14 September.

In the peace treaty of February 1848 Mexico gave up about half its land, from Texas to California, for 15 million dollars. The question of slavery in the new lands split the United States and helped bring on the American Civil War, in which many of Scott's young officers were generals.
